subject: Number of Occasions only reported as 1 for a 45 night survey?

messages.author: 899dbf724565c167
messages.subject: Number of Occasions only reported as 1 for a 45 night survey?
parts:
Hi,

I am busy running a density estimate analysis for spotted hyaena from a 45 night camera trap study with 30 sites. On some days the sites were inactive and I have incorporated this into the 2013trapfile.txt as usage.

Using the below script and the attached two txt files I run the secr.fit function.

CaptHist <- read.capthist("2013RHScaptfile.txt", "2013trapfile.txt", detector="proximity", fmt="trapID", skip = 1)
CaptHist
summary(CaptHist)

fit <- secr.fit (CaptHist, buffer = 8000, trace = FALSE)
fit

My concern is two fold.

1) I receive the warning:
> fit <- secr.fit (CaptHist, buffer = 8000, trace = FALSE)
Warning message:
In bias.D(buffer, temptrps, detectfn = output$detectfn, detectpar = dpar,  :
  bias.D() does not allow for variable effort (detector usage)

Do you know why this might be the case? Do I need to worry about it and how can I address this?

2) When I look at the summary of the fitted model I see the following...
Detector type      count 
Detector number    30 
Average spacing    3020.741 m 
x-range            379440.9 411743.9 m 
y-range            6867394 6893572 m 

 Usage range by occasion
     1
min 41
max 45

N animals       :  79  
N detections    :  159 
N occasions     :  1 
Count model     :  Binomial, size from usage
Mask area       :  117969 ha 

I do not understand why my N Occasions is 1? Surely it should be 45 and will this effect the analysis?

Any advice would be greatly appreciated!

Best,
PJ

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Number of Occasions only reported as 1 for a 45 night survey?
parts:
1. secr.fit() by default runs the function bias.D() as an approximate post-hoc check for truncation bias (buffer too narrow). The check is described briefly at ?bias.D. You can suppress the check with biasLimit = NA. bias.D() does not take 'usage' into account, hence the warning, but this is usually a trivial issue.
2. In recent versions of 'secr' the default for many models is to collapse multi-occasion data to a single occasion (see e.g. secr-version4.pdf). This can be much faster. I regret the confusion it has caused, but the deed is done. Suppress using  details = list(fastproximity = FALSE).
Murray
